mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant for two consecutive months above 5.25%, market expectations for future rate cuts increase, lowering real discount rates and boosting equity present-value pricing, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: FOMC holds rates steady in a restrictive environment
failure_condition: 20-day SPX forward returns in such regimes are not statistically higher than the 30-day rolling mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in hourly wage growth (indirect proxy via UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market, prompting risk-off flows that drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points
regime_hint: Labor market weakening detected via dual indicators
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite sustained labor weakening (IC > 0.05 over 60-day window).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in retail sales ( proxy via HOUST) of at least 3% for three consecutive months predicts stronger near-term consumer demand, which elevates equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥3% month-over-month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 5-day average (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 2% followed by a rebound of >5% the following month indicates a supply shock, which temporarily elevates risk premia and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >2% then rebounds by >5% in consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite the identified pattern (IC < -0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 3.5% while the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL is negative (indicating cooling inflation), it creates a 'soft landing' narrative that supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to the 30-day rolling mean (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 200,000 jobs accompanied by a sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% triggers risk-on flows and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200,000 and UNRATE < 4% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative despite persistent labor market strengthening (IC < -0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for three consecutive months, despite a stable or rising FEDFUNDS rate, suggests the Fed is less concerned about inflation and may pivot to easing, which supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 3.0 for three consecutive months and FEDFUNDS ≥ 5.0 for the same period
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during high-inflation periods (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip in industrial production (INDPRO) — a sharp drop followed by a weaker-than-expected rebound — creates uncertainty about supply chain resilience, which elevates volatility and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% then rebounds by <2% in consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative despite multiple such events over a 6-month window (IC > 0.05).
